question.problem:
Find the Cartesian equation of the osculating plane for a curve $r(t)$ at the point $P(1,0,0)$ where $t=1$, given that

$$
T(1)=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(\,i+\,j),\,N(1)=k.
$$

Note that $T$ and $N$ denote the unit tangent and principal normal, respectively.
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that the position vector of the point $P(1,0,0)$ is $p=⟨1,0,0⟩.$

To find the equation of the osculating plane, we need to find a vector that's perpendicular to it. To do that, we find the cross product of the unit tangent $T(1)$ and the principal normal $N(1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}T(1)\times N(1) & =(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(\,i+\,j))\times k \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}(i-j)\end{aligned}
$$

Since we are interested only in the direction of the above vector, let's write our perpendicular vector $n$ as 

$$
n=\sqrt{2}\cdot (T(1)\times N(1))=i-j=⟨1,-1,0⟩.
$$

Finally, let $⟨x,y,z⟩$ denote the position vector of a general point on the osculating plane. Since the plane is perpendicular to $n$ and passes through the tip of the position vector $p$, its Cartesian equation can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}(⟨x,y,z⟩-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ ⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot n-p\cdot n & =0 \\ ⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ ⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨1,-1,0⟩ & =⟨1,0,0⟩\cdot ⟨1,-1,0⟩ \\ 1\cdot x+(-1)\cdot y+0\cdot z & =1 \\ x-y-1 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
